comma_castle.q:
Choose the correct version:
“My brother a talented pianist won the regional contest.”
opts: My brother, a talented pianist, won
My brother a talented pianist, won
My brother, a talented pianist won
comma_castle.why: An appositive (“a talented pianist”) is extra info — it needs a PAIR of commas, one on each side.

comma_castle.q:
Pick the correctly punctuated list:
“She packed apples pears and plums for the hike.”
comma_castle.why: Items in a series take commas between them. The ACT accepts the Oxford comma — and it never hurts.

comma_castle.q:
Which fixes the comma splice?
“The test was long, I still finished early.”
comma_castle.why: Two complete sentences can’t be glued with just a comma. A semicolon (or period, or comma + and) fixes it.

opts: We visited Paris, France, in May.
We visited Paris France in May.
We visited Paris, France in May.
We visited, Paris France, in May.
comma_castle.why: City, country needs commas around the country name (a paired appositive).
notes: Comma wrongly splits the verb from its object.

vocab_vault.q:

main_idea_meadow.q: The main idea of a passage is:
opts: the point the whole passage makes
main_idea_meadow.why: Main idea covers the whole passage, not one detail.

main_idea_meadow.q: Where does the main idea most often appear?
main_idea_meadow.why: Openers and conclusions usually state the point.

main_idea_meadow.q: A main-idea answer that mentions only one example is probably:
main_idea_meadow.why: One example is too narrow for the whole passage.

main_idea_meadow.q: The best statement of a passage's main idea is one that:
main_idea_meadow.why: Main idea sums up the entire passage, not one detail.
notes: Listing details isn't a main idea.

detail_desert.q: For a detail question about line 15, you should:
detail_desert.why: Detail questions are open-book — go back to the text.

opts: paraphrases the text in new words
detail_desert.why: Right answers restate; exact-word matches are often traps.

detail_desert.q: An answer that changes 'often' to 'always' is wrong because:
detail_desert.why: Extreme words rarely match the text's precise claim.

inference_icefield.q: The best inference is one that is:
opts: barely beyond the text, strongly implied
a bold guess about the future

inference_icefield.q: “She set down the letter and stared out the window.” Best inference:
inference_icefield.why: Smallest supported leap: the letter affected her.

inference_icefield.q: An inference you can't tie to any line is:
inference_icefield.why: Every inference must be provable from the text.
Inferences must be backed by a specific line.
notes: That would be a stated detail, not an inference.

opts: note each author's claim and tone
viewpoint_vista.why: Map each author so you can compare accurately.

viewpoint_vista.q: A question asks where both authors AGREE. You should:
opts: find a point supported by BOTH
viewpoint_vista.why: Agreement answers must hold for both passages.

viewpoint_vista.q: The biggest risk in paired passages is:

graph_gorge.q: With several curves on one graph, you should:
opts: use the legend and follow one labeled curve

graph_gorge.q: Where two curves intersect, the quantities are:
graph_gorge.why: An intersection means the values are equal there.

graph_gorge.q: The most common graph error is:
graph_gorge.why: Mixing up x and y is the classic mistake.

experiment_expanse.q: The variable the researchers deliberately change is the:
The purpose of a control group is to:
experiment_expanse.why: The control isolates the treatment's effect.

experiment_expanse.q: If two variables change between trials, you:
opts: can't tell which caused the result
experiment_expanse.why: Only one variable should change to isolate a cause.

conflict_canyon.why: A one-line summary of each view guides every question.

conflict_canyon.q: New evidence supporting cause A most likely:
opts: strengthens the scientist who argued A
conflict_canyon.why: Match evidence to the viewpoint it supports.

conflict_canyon.q: In a conflicting-viewpoints passage, the key is usually:
opts: the point where the scientists disagree
conflict_canyon.why: Questions hinge on the disagreement between views.
notes: Captions rarely hold the core dispute.
